bib.title: Adapting the Interface, Not the Model: Runtime Harness Adaptation for Deterministic LLM Agents

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Adapting the Interface, Not the Model: Runtime Harness Adaptation for Deterministic LLM Agents" (system name LIFE-HARNESS), Tianshi Xu, Huifeng Wen (equal contribution), Meng Li, Peking University. Preprint, arXiv:2605.22166v3 [cs.AI], dated 15 Oct 2026. No venue stated. Code on GitHub (URL not in the extraction).

COVERAGE: Read all 21 of 21 pages (83,937 of 83,937 chars): body, limitations, references, appendices A to C, Tables 1-13. Tables 10-13 are dense numeric tables. I read them but did not quote them all. Figure 3, 5 and 7 numbers are scrambled in the extraction, so I did not quote them.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- LIFE-HARNESS lifts a frozen Qwen3-4B-Instruct on seven AgentBench and tau-bench environments, with no weight changes.
  number: AgentBench mean Pass@1 27.9 to 59.5. tau suites mean Pass@1 36.3 to 71.0.
  setup: Qwen3-4B-Instruct is the frozen solver. GPT-5.5 is the evolution LLM. Six evolution rounds, batches of up to 50 training tasks, temperature 0.0. Test sets are held out: ALFWorld 109, DBBench 300, OS 144, WebShop 200, Airline 20, Retail 40, Telecom 40 (Table 5). The tau results use 3 runs per task. AgentBench uses a single run.
  quote: "improves mean Pass@1 accuracy from 27.9% to 59.5% on AgentBench and from 36.3% to 71.0% across the two τ suites, achieving the highest accuracy on five of seven environments."
  where: p.7, Table 1

- It beats the two automated harness-search baselines on accuracy and on evolution tokens.
  number: +28.7 pp over Meta-Harness, +7.5 pp over AHE. 8.5% fewer evolution tokens than Meta-Harness, 68.4% fewer than AHE.
  setup: Same solver, evolution LLM, rollout settings and 6 rounds. Mean over the 7 shared environments. Table 1 means across all 7 environments: LIFE 64.45 (abstract), Meta-Harness and AHE per-suite means as printed in Table 1.
  quote: "LIFE-HARNESSexceeds Meta-Harness and AHE by 28.7 and 7.5 percentage points in mean accuracy, respectively, while using 8.5% fewer evolution tokens than Meta-Harness and 68.4% fewer than AHE."
  where: p.7
  caveat: AHE wins on ALFWorld (89.0 vs 88.1) and Telecom (95.0 vs 90.0). Per Table 12, accuracy is measured on each round's training batch. Each method is a single run per environment, with no confidence intervals.

- One evolved harness transfers across 18 open-weight backbones. It gains least on models that are already strong.
  number: improved 132 of 144 settings across all 8 environments (including AppWorld). 116 of 126 on the 7 AgentBench and tau environments. AppWorld mean 25.5 to 30.8, improved on 16 of 18 backbones (Table 3). The abstract rounds this to +5.3 pp.
  setup: Harness evolved on Qwen3-4B-Instruct, reused unchanged. The backbones are Qwen2.5, Qwen3, Qwen3.5, Qwen3.6, Llama 3.1/3.3 and xLAM-2.
  quote: "improving132 of 144model–environment settings across all eight environments."
  where: p.3, p.7, Tables 3, 10, 13
  note: Table 10 shows big gains on weak models (Qwen3-4B ALFWorld 16.5 to 88.1, Llama-3.1-8B ALFWorld 5.5 to 82.6). Qwen3.5-27B and Qwen3.6-27B gain little or lose a little on several tau environments. Llama-3.3-70B Telecom 30.8 to 33.3, with little change on Retail.

- The harness also helps three frontier models, at a smaller size.
  number: +2.8 (GPT 5.5), +4.4 (Opus 4.8), +3.4 (Gemini 3.1 Pro) pp mean. Gains in 18 of 21 model-environment settings. The abstract gives an average of 3.5 pp.
  setup: Seven environments, harness evolved on Qwen3-4B and frozen, "High" setting for GPT 5.5 and Opus 4.8. Table 2 examples: Retail Opus 72.5 to 84.2, DBBench GPT 5.5 67.7 to 75.0. It lost on OS for Gemini (50.0 to 48.6) and was flat on GPT Retail (72.5 to 72.5), Gemini ALFWorld (96.3 to 96.3) and Opus OS (50.4 to 50.8).
  quote: "LIFE-HARNESSimproves accuracy by 2.8, 4.4, and 3.4 pp, respectively, with gains in 18 of 21 model–environment settings."
  where: p.8, Table 2

- Diagnosis. Most failures of the 4B solver are interface mismatches, not reasoning errors. The share varies by environment.
  number: 393 failed training episodes. The Figure 3a pie shows 23.2%, 33.3%, 33.6%, 9.9% across four categories. The label-to-percent mapping is scrambled in the extraction, so I cannot attribute which is which. Verified from text: general reasoning is the residual category.
  setup: Frozen Qwen3-4B-Instruct on training tasks. Primary failure type is the earliest dominant bottleneck, annotated by an LLM and checked by human reviewers. Priority order: action realization, then environment contract, then trajectory degeneration, then residual reasoning.
  quote: "deterministic agent failures are heterogeneous: all four categories occur in practice, and the dominant mode varies substantially across environments."
  where: p.4, App. A.1
  motivating contrast (intro): "Qwen3.5-4B achieves 74.0% on HMMT Feb ... but only 43.1% on ALFWorld"

- Each of the four layers matters, but which one matters depends on the environment.
  number: Leave-one-layer-out relative accuracy drops. Removing Action Realization: Airline -61.7%, OS -59.6%. Removing Trajectory Regulation: ALFWorld -86.5%, Telecom -36.2%, WebShop -26.4%. Removing Contract: Retail -17.5%, DBBench -16.9%. Removing Skill: Telecom -17.4%, Retail -15.9% (smallest, e.g. DBBench -3.1%, ALFWorld -1.0%).
  setup: Qwen3-4B-Instruct, drops relative to the full harness.
  quote: "Removing any harness layer causes substantial accuracy drops on some benchmarks. The impact varies across environments"
  where: p.8, Table 4
  note: Removal only, with no adding-one-at-a-time and no confidence intervals.

- Prompt-only optimization is not enough. LIFE-HARNESS beat a prompt-evolving baseline on all seven environments.
  number: none (Figure 6 bars only, not extractable).
  setup: Qwen3-4B-Instruct, compared with GEPA-style and OPRO-style prompt optimization (Agrawal 2025; Yang 2024a).
  quote: "LIFE-HARNESSachieves higher Pass@1 accuracy across all seven environments."
  where: p.7-8, Fig. 6

- It stacks on top of model-side tool training.
  number: gains of +14.6, +20.0 and +34.2 pp for xLAM-2-32B (read off the figure labels, ordering scrambled in extraction). Qwen2.5-32B plus the harness exceeds the original xLAM-2-32B on tau-bench by 7.5 pp.
  quote: "On τ-bench, Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct equipped with LIFE-HARNESSalso exceeds the original xLAM-2-32B by 7.5 pp."
  where: p.8, Fig. 7
  note: the pairing of the Fig. 7 gains with groups is unreliable.

- It beats two released environment-interface baselines (ALIGN, AgentSquare) on ALFWorld and WebShop.
  number: Qwen3-4B ALFWorld: w/o 16.51, ALIGN 28.36, AgentSquare 29.36, LIFE 88.07. WebShop: 29.50, 18.00, 18.50, 45.50.
  setup: 18 backbones. ALIGN uses its released task split. AgentSquare uses the LIFE task selection. These are not run under the same evolution conditions. The authors just evaluated the released harnesses.
  quote: "LIFE-HARNESSoutperforms both methods across all backbones on ALFWorld and in most settings on WebShop."
  where: p.8, Table 11
  note: ALIGN and AgentSquare often score below no-harness (e.g. WebShop Qwen3-4B 18.00 vs 29.50).

- The method, usable as an anatomy of a harness. Four lifecycle layers, each at a different point in the loop.
  1) Environment Contract Layer, before interaction: makes tool-use rules, policy constraints and pitfalls explicit, via enhanced contract C' = C plus delta.
  2) Procedural Skill Layer, at task conditioning: BM25 retrieval over skills distilled from training trajectories, inserted in the system prompt.
  3) Action Realization Layer, between model output and execution: returns EXEC or BLOCK(message). It validates, canonicalizes unambiguous interface errors, and blocks calls that would deterministically fail.
  4) Trajectory Regulation Layer, after feedback: detects repetition, stagnation, invalid retries, budget exhaustion, and appends a recovery message.
  quote: "Many agent failures are self-reinforcing: the agent repeats the same invalid command, loops between equivalent states, or exhausts the budget without making progress."
  where: p.4-6, Algorithm 1
  also: Only the top-1 retrieved skill is used, "preventing irrelevant skills from contaminating the model context" (App. B).

- Evolution loop. An evolution LLM reads training trajectories and the current harness and proposes edits. Candidates pass replay and interface checks, with up to 3 repair attempts. A candidate is accepted only on a strict accuracy gain on the same training batch.
  quote: "accepts only a strict accuracy improvement."
  where: p.6, p.12-13, App. A.2
  note: Table 12 shows accuracy on training batches that differ per round (50 tasks, so noisy). DBBench goes 72 to 58 to 56 to 70, and Retail 48 to 30 to 50, so round-to-round numbers are noisy, as the batch changes.

LIMITS
- The authors concede one limit: "Our evaluation covers text- and API-based agent environments." Visual GUI tasks (desktop, mobile) are left to future work.
- The scope is deterministic, rule-governed environments. The harness is environment-specific but model-agnostic, so it must be re-evolved per environment. Whether it helps open-ended domains such as coding or browsing is not shown.
- Small tau test sets (Airline n=20, Retail n=40, Telecom n=40). One evolution run per method, no seeds or confidence intervals. Three-run Pass@1/Pass3 for tau only.
- The harness is evolved on a 4B solver with GPT-5.5 as the evolution LLM. The cost counts only evolution LLM tokens (Table 12 note), not solver or evaluation tokens.
- The evolved harness contains heavily environment-specific code (Tables 7-9, e.g. a full WorldModel for ALFWorld, SQL dialect repair and "tool-call rescue" for DBBench). This leaves open how much of the gain is domain engineering, as opposed to generic structure.
- The tau user simulator is DeepSeek-V4-Flash. AppWorld gains are small (mean 25.5 to 30.8).
- Frontier gains are small and mixed. Some settings are flat or negative.
- Some LLM-annotated failure labels were human-checked, but the paper gives no agreement statistics.

BUILDS ON
- Meta-Harness (Lee et al., 2026, arXiv:2603.28052) and Agentic Harness Engineering / AHE (Lin et al., 2026, arXiv:2604.25850) are the direct baselines for automated harness evolution. The note already cites both.
- ADAS (Hu et al., 2025), AFlow (Zhang et al., 2025), AgentSquare (Shang et al., 2025), ALIGN (Liu et al., 2025), WALL-E (Zhou et al., 2025).
- Prompt optimizers: PromptWizard, OPRO (Yang et al., 2024a), TextGrad, GEPA (Agrawal et al., 2025), ACE (Zhang et al., 2026b).
- Benchmarks: AgentBench (Liu et al., 2024), tau-bench (Yao et al., 2024), tau2-bench (Barres et al., 2025), AppWorld (Trivedi et al., 2024), ALFWorld, WebShop.
- Concurrent: HarnessX (Chen et al., 2026), AutoHarness (Lou et al., 2026), Self-Harness (Zhang et al., 2026a), Continual Harness (Karten et al., 2026), Harbor (Sengupta and Wang, 2026).
- SWE-agent (Yang et al., 2024b) is cited for agent-computer interfaces.

CODE: no code in the paper. Only the pseudocode in Algorithm 1 (p.6) and the evolution prompt template in App. A.2. Core loop: REALIZEACTION returns EXEC(a_t) or BLOCK(m_t); REGULATETRAJECTORY returns an appended recovery message.

FIGURES (via captions only; I did not render images)
- Fig. 2 (p.2): "(a) An agent is not just an LLM: its behavior is shaped by the runtime harness that mediates observations, tools, actions, and feedback. (b) We adapt this runtime interface, rather than model parameters." Contrasts parameter adaptation (retrain per model) with one reusable harness.
- Fig. 4 (p.5): overview of the four layers placed before interaction, at task conditioning, before execution and after execution. The quickest explanation of the lifecycle layers.
- Fig. 3 (p.4): failure diagnosis, overall and per-environment pies and bars.
- Fig. 5 (p.7): per-backbone gain heatmap across 18 models and 7 benchmarks.
- Tables 7-9 (p.15-17): concrete inventory of what each layer contains per environment. Useful as examples of contract, skill, action and trajectory components.

RELEVANCE TO NOTE 02-harness-anatomy (observations only)
- The paper's four-layer cut (contract / skill / action realization / trajectory regulation) maps roughly onto the note's subsystems: contract and skill to Instructions and Tools, action realization to hooks and middleware (the deterministic shell), trajectory regulation to Feedback. This mapping is my reading, not stated in the paper.
- It supports the note's claim that reliability requirements belong in the deterministic shell: Table 4 shows removing Action Realization drops Airline -61.7% and OS -59.6%.
- It extends the note's AHE and Meta-Harness ablation paragraph with a removal ablation in a different domain (deterministic environments).
- Direct comparison with AHE on the shared baseline: LIFE is +7.5 pp over AHE on the seven shared environments.

PROBLEMS
- Extraction of Figures 3, 5 and 7 is scrambled, so those numbers are unreliable.
- Tables 1 and 10 have bolding artifacts. For Table 1, columns read as "w/o | Meta-Harness | AHE | Life-Harness" with Acc and Cost for each. Some cells run together, e.g. "3.789.09.6 88.12.4" is AHE ALFWorld 89.0 (cost 9.6) and LIFE 88.1 (cost 2.4), with Meta-Harness cost 3.7. The cost unit is 10^7 tokens.
- Table 1 reports AHE Telecom 95.0, Pass3 87.5. The row "Mean Pass@1 27.9 38.6 3.3 55.7 9.9 59.5 2.5" is AgentBench: w/o 27.9, Meta 38.6, AHE 55.7, LIFE 59.5.
- The abstract says Qwen3-4B "28.7 and 7.5" over Meta-Harness and AHE. Table 1's tau means (36.3, 31.9, 58.6, 71.0) and AgentBench means imply those margins. I did not recompute them.
- Dates are in the future relative to my training, so I cannot check the models named (GPT 5.5, Opus 4.8, Gemini 3.1 Pro). I took them as printed.
- No embedded instructions found in the PDF text.
